name: Earth Pro
subtitle: Desktop Globe & KML Maps
promotionalText: Explore a tiled globe, organize KML projects, plot address lists, compare dated imagery, and discover public data around your view. Native mapping for your Mac.
description:
Keep your map projects on the desktop.

Earth Pro is an independent, native Mac mapping workspace for exploring a globe, organizing places, measuring land, and working with your own geographic data. Start with Apple Maps, OpenStreetMap, or the tiled globe without a Google API key.

PLOT AND ORGANIZE YOUR PLACES
Search with location suggestions and fly to a highlighted pin. Paste up to 250 addresses to plot a list, review unresolved matches, and style pins with colors, shapes, icons, and notes. Organize saved places and custom layers in folders. Import KML/KMZ and export supported places as KML.

EXPLORE WITH MORE DETAIL
Stream tiled globe imagery as you zoom. Use selectable measurement units and decimal precision for distance, perimeter, and area. See coordinates, approximate elevation, eye altitude, and imagery dates where the source supplies them.

COMPARE IMAGERY OVER TIME
Browse NASA daily satellite history and Esri World Imagery Wayback releases. View location-specific capture dates when available. Archive release dates and image capture dates are identified separately; history coverage varies.

BRING YOUR DATA TO THE MAP
Use Places, Layers, and Data tabs to organize work, control visibility, and discover sources around the current view or a chosen area. Find public parcels, zoning, flood mapping, and utility datasets where available. Import supported local data or connect custom sources. Source metadata shows supplied update dates and identifies missing dates honestly. Coverage and reuse terms vary by publisher.

CAPTURE AND CONNECT
Position image overlays, adjust opacity, save map images, and record silent map videos. A local, authenticated MCP server lets compatible AI clients use supported navigation, places, notes, layers, data imports, source dates, overlays, and recording tools. Local MCP starts enabled and can be switched off; its session token is required.

OPTIONAL GOOGLE MAPS
Add your own compatible Google Maps API key for Google imagery and photorealistic 3D buildings and terrain where supported. The key is stored in macOS Keychain. Google may charge separately for API usage.

Requires macOS 14 or later. Online maps, search, source discovery, and remote imagery require internet access. No Earth Pro account is required. Measurement, elevation, address matching, and provider coverage have practical limits; this app is not a survey instrument.

Earth Pro is independently developed and is not affiliated with Google. It offers a desktop workflow as Google Earth Pro downloads wind down; it does not duplicate every Google Earth feature. Original app code is MIT licensed. Provider imagery and third-party data retain their own terms.

Open-source code (MIT); included data/services are not cleared for commercial use as-is. The free Open-Meteo elevation API permits noncommercial use only. Commercial deployments must replace or properly license restricted services and comply with each data and imagery provider’s terms. These limits concern third-party content/services, not the MIT code grant. See https://zachenson.com/earth-pro/terms.
reviewNotes:
Earth Pro 1.0 (build 6) replaces build 5 and includes updated sidebar organization, smoother tiled globe imagery, NASA/Wayback history, public/custom data layers, location notes, source dates, and expanded MCP tools. No app account or Google API key is needed for review: start with Globe, Apple Maps, or OpenStreetMap.

REQUIRED NETWORK.SERVER ENTITLEMENT
This app implements two incoming TCP listeners, both bound explicitly to 127.0.0.1 only. network.client does not permit these listeners.
1. Local MCP: Tools > Local MCP Control (or network toolbar icon). The persisted setting defaults ON. The panel shows status, the per-session bearer token and Copy LLM Prompt. An MCP client can connect to http://127.0.0.1:18794/mcp, initialize, list tools, and navigate/manage supported map data. A request without the bearer token returns HTTP 401. Turning local control off stops the listener. No cloud LLM account is required; Earth Pro does not itself transmit state to an LLM.
2. Google Maps viewer: choosing Google Maps with a user key starts the internal viewer server on 127.0.0.1:18793. WKWebView loads a bundled page at a random path to establish an HTTP origin/referrer. This endpoint does not serve the key or the saved-place library. It is not exposed to LAN/public interfaces. Google Maps/photorealistic 3D are optional BYO-key features; Google may charge separately.

REVIEW WALKTHROUGH
Search a public address, select a result to fly to its pin, and save/style it. Add > Plot Address List accepts one address per line and reports duplicates/unresolved matches. Places organizes items in folders; right-click a saved item for Fly To, Edit, Notes, Move, Export and Delete. Layers controls visibility; layer actions include Restore default layers. Data follows the map or a chosen area, and imports/connects custom sources. Geometry loads only when added/enabled at a useful view scale; public-data coverage varies. Source update dates are shown only when supplied.
History toolbar: NASA daily satellite imagery and Esri Wayback archive releases; capture dates are separate from archive release dates. Neither is Google's historical aerial archive. Image overlays support bounds, rotation and opacity. Video captures map views silently. Help provides support and privacy links.

Existing automated entitlement issue: please test both local listeners above; they are implemented app functionality requiring network.server. Original code is MIT licensed, and map services/data retain provider terms. There are no user accounts, public posting, in-app purchases or social messaging.

LICENSE NOTICE
Open-source code (MIT); included data/services are not cleared for commercial use as-is. The free Open-Meteo elevation API permits noncommercial use only. Commercial deployments must replace or properly license restricted services and comply with each data and imagery provider’s terms. These limits concern third-party content/services, not the MIT code grant. See https://zachenson.com/earth-pro/terms. Help > License & Data Usage and About explain this boundary.
